newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar firms at close after political comments.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar firms at close after political comments.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended slightly firmer at the close on Tuesday after political comments were construed as being mildly bullish for the currency.
Earlier in the session, newly-appointed Treasurer Winston Peters said that the speed of the currency's rise was a concern.
But coalition partner and Prime Minister Jim Bolger later said a strong dollar was not necessarily bad and that it simply reflected a strong economy.
"The market was caught a little off guard really. They were expecting the (post-cabinet) comments to be bearish. Infact, the comments could be seen as neutral to marginally bullish," said one dealer.
Overnight, bids were expected to be limited to US$0.7050 and offers at 0.7080. Stiff resistance was expected at the figure.
"There was a reasonable chance for the Kiwi to come off today and it held in quite nicely," the dealer said.
At the close, Kiwi was at 0.7057/64 and at 68.57 on the Trade Weighted Index from 0.7055/62 and 68.62 early in the day's trade.
Focus is now turning to Thursday's GDP data, which will prove a guide as to whether the market's opinions on inflationary pressures are justified.
Until the release, tight trading ranges were expected.
